text:
Toronto got its two goals in the first 12 minutes and then spent the rest of the night leaning on Anthony Stolarz. By the end, NYI had thrown 68 shot attempts to TOR's 48 and held a slight edge in how the game was played, deserving the win 53 percent of the time. The Maple Leafs held on anyway, 2-1.

The first period was entirely Toronto's. The Leafs out-chanced NYI 1.24 to 0.44 in expected goals, and it showed on the board. Colton Sissons tipped one in at 7:14, assisted by Nick Paul and Easton Cowan. Cowan then made it 2-0 at 11:55 with a wrist shot on the power play, a 36 percent chance, with Jack Roslovic and Morgan Rielly drawing the assists. Toronto converted one of its four power plays, creating 1.06 expected goals with the man advantage, while NYI went 0 for 4.

From there the game tilted the other way. NYI won the second period 0.95 to 0.65 in expected goals and the third 1.27 to 0.80, and Toronto blocked 21 shots to NYI's 11 to stay ahead. Stolarz stopped 26 of 27, saving 1.67 goals more than the chances against him called for, and he turned away Kyle Palmieri on a 21 percent look in the third. Emil Heineman did beat him shorthanded at 14:09 of the third, a snap shot assisted by Bo Horvat, but NYI could not find the equalizer. Ilya Sorokin was fine at the other end, giving up two on 2.49 expected.
